questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the official language of the country was English. That the climate was different from the danish. That it was outside of Europe. That the location made traveling possible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had a very good experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it to be pretty structured in terms of what steps to do at specific times. But there was still a lot to remember and if you missed a step the process was quite long.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most assistance was online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They have a loot of different websites and apps that can be hard to manage.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Student collages and student halls. 
I stayed at a student hall that was a very social option but not the most luxurious.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Either meal plan was mandatory or the housing had provided a kitchen, but even with a kitchen they did not have any kitchen equipment so it was easier and cheaper to buy food at the food stalls on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Some does not have aircon that can be tought sometimes. Most people get used to it, but it is very hot in Singapore especially at night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was hot without aircon and if you had clothes hanging in the room that wasn't washed for a while mold would grow on it because of the humidity. But I really enjoyed the social activities and the 'højskole' vibe at the hall with breakfast and dinner included, even though it wasn't the best food.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There is different rounds of course registration. 
The first one is from home and then there is a period when you arrive where it is possible to change courses that is based on your priorities. They do not allow overlaps in the course schedule so it was a bit of a puzzle.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to contact the administration for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful, but I was not able to secure all the courses I wanted because of availability and schedule overlap.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just relax if it doesn't work out as you want in the first place and make a long list with all the courses you are interested in because you will not be able to secure exactly what you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level compared to the level at University of Copenhagen, but they are quite generous with final grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot more deadlines throughout the semester and the grades is based on a lot of different things and not just your final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Metabolism and Regulation 
Synthetic Biology 
RNA biology and technology 
Introduction to bioinformatics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed all of my courses. 
Metabolism and regulation has a high workload but is interesting if you are interested in metabolic diseases. Synthetic Biology was more easy and they were generous with the grades, a lot of exchange students as well. RNA biology and technology was very interesting and not too hard to pass either but did contain a lot of details. Introduction to bioinformatics was not that interesting but not hard to pass either.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Supplies for the room

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
going out and eating at restaurants is expensive in Singapore. The public transport is cheap but doesn't leave at night so you needed to pay taxi.
I spend most money on traveling, the everyday life in Singapore was not expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of different sports to participate in. It is not made for exchange students but more for the local students that gain participation points when joining different clubs. This means that it is not a chill drop-in and out vibe, but you have to commit if you join anything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining one club either a certain sport you enjoy or something more creative.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
To go traveling to the neighboring countries. You can go by bus and ferry to Malaysia and indonesia. 
Also make sure to go to the different areas of Singapore in the beginning as you start to get more busy throughout the semester and there is a lot of good things to experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a bit of a culture shock at first with all the different noises, smells and climate. And as an asian country it is very different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club and live on campus it is hard to socialize at uni.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The all year summer.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open and enjoy it, it is a very unique time. And be prepared that it is hard at some points to be so far away from home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Consider having an international bank account, you will end up using cash a lot. 
Pack some personal things from home to place in your room and remember that you need less clothes than you think.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
All the people I met and became friends with. 
And all the travel experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was hard to socialize at the some of the courses and everyone has different schedules so you will be alone quite a lot in your everyday life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange! you will not regret it

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
